basis_legend.evidenced: visible in the live AdventureWorks2022 data, FKs, triggers or procs
basis_legend.inferred: what the data implies a business would do, not provable from the DB

processes.name: Order-to-cash: internet (B2C)
processes.summary: An individual customer browses, fills a cart, checks out with a credit card; the order is approved, picked from finished-goods stock, shipped by truck ground and settled on the card.
processes.trigger: Shopper places an order on the web site (OnlineOrderFlag = 1).

steps.name: Browse catalog
steps.note: Only sellable products (SellEndDate null).

steps.name: Add to cart
steps.note: Cart table exists but holds only 3 rows: carts are transient.

steps.name: Check out (address, card, ship method)
steps.note: Every internet order uses XRQ - TRUCK GROUND; DueDate = OrderDate + 12 days; ~46% carry a currency rate (foreign-currency web shop).

steps.name: Ask why the shopper bought (sales reasons)
steps.note: Survey-style reasons (Price dominates). AdventureWorksDW models them as internet-only (FactInternetSalesReason).

steps.name: Authorise card
steps.note: Approval code column exists; there is no payment / settlement table, so capture and settlement are outside the DB.

steps.name: Approve and pick
steps.note: Trigger iduSalesOrderDetail writes one TransactionHistory row of type S per order line: S rows (current+archive) = order lines exactly. It does NOT decrement ProductInventory.

steps.name: Ship
steps.note: Every historical order is Shipped; ShipDate = OrderDate + 7 days for all internet orders; no carrier tracking on internet lines.

steps.name: Invoice / collect
steps.note: TotalDue is a computed column; there is no invoice, payment or AR table. Cash side lives only in DW FactFinance (static).

processes.state_diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> InProcess: checkout (status 1)
    InProcess --> Approved: card authorised / credit ok (2)
    InProcess --> Rejected: card declined (4)
    InProcess --> Cancelled: shopper cancels (6)
    Approved --> Backordered: no stock (3)
    Backordered --> Approved: stock arrives
    Approved --> Shipped: ShipDate set (5)
    Shipped --> [*]
    Rejected --> [*]
    Cancelled --> [*]
    note right of Shipped: evidenced - all 27,659 internet orders are status 5\nother states come from ufnGetSalesOrderStatusText (inferred transitions)
processes.flowchart:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Shopper
    A([Browse catalog]) --> B[Add to cart] --> C[Checkout: address, card, ship method]
    C --> R[Pick sales reasons]
  end
  subgraph Storefront
    C --> D[(SalesOrderHeader + Details\nstatus 1)]
    D --> E{Card approved?}
  end
  subgraph Fulfilment
    E -- yes --> F[Approve, status 2] --> G{In stock?}
    G -- no --> H[Backorder, status 3] --> G
    G -- yes --> I[Pick: TransactionHistory S] --> J[Ship: ShipDate, status 5]
  end
  E -- no --> K[Reject, status 4]
  J --> L([Invoice / settle - outside DB])

evidence.note: every internet order is Shipped: the DB holds only completed history
of 27,659; the rest have no card on file
S rows = 121,317 = SalesOrderDetail rows: one stock-out transaction per order line

gaps: No back-office order screen: orders stay at status 1 forever; SAL-05 (orders by status) and SAL-06 (ship/cancel/revise) are designed but no page uses them.
Checkout uses flat demo tax (8%) and freight (2.5%) instead of Sales.SalesTaxRate (REF-02) and ShipMethod rates (REF-04).
No special-offer pricing at checkout (CAT-10 designed, unused).
Sales reasons are not captured at checkout (SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason only arrives via CDC for SQL orders).
No stock check / stock movement on order: SQL wrote TransactionHistory type S per line; DynamoDB checkout writes nothing to aw-inventory (INV-03 unused).
No multi-currency: CurrencyRate (REF-03) is loaded but the shop prices in USD only.
Payment, invoice and cash receipt have no OLTP tables at all (gap in the source schema, not just the app).

processes.name: Order-to-cash: reseller (B2B)
processes.summary: A sales person takes an order from a reseller store against the store's purchase order number; volume discounts apply; the order ships by cargo with carrier tracking per line and counts toward the sales person's quota.
processes.trigger: Reseller sends a purchase order to its assigned sales person (OnlineOrderFlag = 0, PurchaseOrderNumber set).

steps.name: Receive reseller PO
steps.note: Contacts typed Purchasing Agent / Purchasing Manager (487 of 909) are the store's buyers.

steps.note: All 3,806 reseller orders have a sales person and a PO number; 0 internet orders do.

steps.name: Apply volume / reseller promotions
steps.note: 3,282 discounted reseller lines; Volume Discount 11-14 alone is on 3,428 lines.

steps.name: Credit approval (card or terms)
steps.note: 3,799 of 3,806 reseller orders carry a card id; terms/credit limit do not exist in the schema.

steps.name: Pick and ship with tracking
steps.note: Every reseller line has a carrier tracking number; all ship by CARGO TRANSPORT 5.

steps.name: Revise order
steps.note: Trigger uSalesOrderHeader bumps RevisionNumber; 30 orders are at revision 9 (one extra revision) vs 8 for the rest.

steps.name: Credit sales person / territory YTD
steps.note: Stored YTD aggregates exist; nothing in the DB maintains them (probably a batch).

processes.name: Procure-to-pay
processes.summary: A buyer raises a purchase order to an approved vendor for a purchased component; the PO is approved, goods are received (with quality rejects) into stock, and the vendor is paid.
actors: Buyer (12 distinct employees: Buyer, Purchasing Assistant, Purchasing Manager)
processes.trigger: Stock of a purchased product (MakeFlag = 0) falls below ReorderPoint, or a work order needs components (inferred).

steps.name: Detect need (below reorder point)
steps.note: 60 sellable products are below reorder point today; nothing in the DB links a PO to that signal.

steps.name: Choose vendor
steps.note: 460 product-vendor offers for 265 products; 93 of 104 vendors preferred.

steps.name: Raise PO
steps.note: Trigger iPurchaseOrderDetail recalculates SubTotal and writes TransactionHistory type P.

steps.name: Approve / reject
steps.note: uPurchaseOrderHeader bumps RevisionNumber; revisions 4..20 show repeated edits.

steps.name: Vendor ships
steps.note: ShipDate = OrderDate + 9 days on 4,000 of 4,012 POs.

steps.name: Receive and inspect
steps.note: 380 lines partially received; 563 lines with rejects; 72,700 units rejected of 2.33M received.

steps.name: Put away
steps.note: No trigger moves stock into ProductInventory on receipt.

steps.name: Close PO / pay vendor
steps.note: No invoice, 3-way-match or payment table.

processes.state_diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending: PO raised (1)
    Pending --> Approved: manager approves (2)
    Pending --> Rejected: manager rejects (3)
    Pending --> Pending: edit (RevisionNumber+1)
    Approved --> Complete: all lines received (4)
    Approved --> Approved: partial receipt
    Complete --> [*]
    Rejected --> [*]
    note right of Pending: evidenced distribution 225 / 12 / 86 / 3,689\nreceipt quantities do not respect status (synthetic data)
processes.flowchart:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Buyer
    A([Stock below reorder point]) --> B[Pick vendor: ProductVendor\nlead time, price, preferred]
    B --> C[Raise PO, status 1]
  end
  subgraph Manager
    C --> D{Approve?}
  end
  D -- no --> R[Rejected, status 3]
  D -- yes --> E[Approved, status 2]
  subgraph Vendor
    E --> F[Ship: ShipDate = +9d]
  end
  subgraph Receiving
    F --> G[Receive: ReceivedQty]
    G --> H{Inspection}
    H -- reject --> I[RejectedQty]
    H -- accept --> J[StockedQty → TransactionHistory P\nput away to ProductInventory]
  end
  J --> K{All received?}
  K -- no --> G
  K -- yes --> L[Complete, status 4] --> M([AP pays - outside DB])

evidence.note: pending/rejected POs show receipts: status is not consistent with receipts, so the transitions are inferred

redshift: landed in Redshift via zero-ETL but no purchasing fact or report (AdventureWorksDW has none)

gaps: Entire process has no UI: all 7 PUR patterns are designed and load-tested but unused by the app.
No approval workflow, receiving or inspection screen; StockedQty never reaches ProductInventory in either system.
No purchasing analytics (spend by vendor, vendor on-time / reject rate) in Redshift.
No reorder suggestion linking INV-02 (below reorder point) to PUR-02 (who can supply).

processes.name: Plan-to-produce (work orders, BOM, routing, scrap)
processes.summary: Production planning releases a work order for a manufactured product; it is routed through up to 7 work centres (frame forming → final assembly), consumes components per the bill of materials, and stocks finished units with some scrap.
processes.trigger: Demand or stock for a MakeFlag = 1 product (inferred: no link from sales orders to work orders).

steps.name: Explode bill of materials
steps.note: 238 assemblies, up to 5 levels (BOMLevel 0-4); 199 BOM edges end-dated (engineering changes). uspGetBillOfMaterials / uspGetWhereUsedProductID.

steps.name: Release work order
steps.note: Trigger iWorkOrder writes a type-W transaction: W rows (current+archive) = 72,591 = work orders exactly.

steps.name: Schedule routing operations
steps.note: 42,625 work orders are routed; OperationSequence 1-7 maps to the 7 work-centre locations.

steps.name: Execute operations
steps.note: 39,212 operations finished after ScheduledEndDate; ActualCost = PlannedCost in total (synthetic).

steps.name: Issue components
steps.note: No component-issue transaction type exists; consumption is not recorded.

steps.name: Record scrap
steps.note: 729 work orders with scrap, 10,651 units, 16 reasons fairly evenly used.

steps.name: Complete and stock
steps.note: All 72,591 work orders are closed; 22,790 closed after DueDate.

processes.state_entity: Production.WorkOrder (derived from StartDate / EndDate / DueDate; no status column)
processes.state_diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Released: WorkOrder insert (+TransactionHistory W)
    Released --> InOperation: routing op 1 ActualStartDate
    InOperation --> InOperation: next OperationSequence
    InOperation --> Scrapped: ScrappedQty / ScrapReasonID
    Scrapped --> InOperation
    InOperation --> ClosedOnTime: EndDate <= DueDate
    InOperation --> ClosedLate: EndDate > DueDate
    ClosedOnTime --> [*]
    ClosedLate --> [*]
    note right of Released: derived states - no Status column; 0 open today
processes.flowchart:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Planning
    A([Demand for make product]) --> B[Explode BOM\nmulti-level, as-of date]
    B --> C[Release WorkOrder\n+TransactionHistory W]
    C --> D[Schedule routing\nops 1..7 by Location]
  end
  subgraph floor[Shop floor]
    D --> E[Frame Forming / Welding / Debur / Paint]
    E --> F[Subassembly] --> G[Final Assembly]
    G --> H{Quality check}
  end
  H -- defect --> S[Scrap: ScrapReason]
  H -- pass --> I[EndDate, StockedQty\nFinished Goods Storage]

access_patterns.question: Explode the bill of materials for an assembly (all levels, as of a date)
Where is this component used?

redshift: none: AdventureWorksDW has no manufacturing fact; WorkOrder items land in Redshift via zero-ETL only

gaps: No production UI: BOM explosion (INV-04), where-used (INV-05) and work-order/routing (INV-06) are designed but unused.
No work-order status column: open/late must be derived from dates (the design uses a sparse index on open WOs).
No component consumption (backflush) and no link from sales demand to work orders in either system.
No production KPIs (on-time rate, scrap rate by reason, planned vs actual cost) in Redshift.

processes.name: Inventory management
processes.summary: Stock is held per product per location (14 locations, shelf/bin); every sale, purchase receipt and work order writes a stock transaction; old transactions are archived; reorder points and safety stock drive replenishment.
processes.trigger: Any stock movement (sale S, purchase P, work order W) or a periodic stock review.

steps.note: S = sales lines, W = work orders, P = PO receipts; written by triggers, not by users.

steps.name: Adjust on-hand per location/bin
steps.note: Nothing links transactions to ProductInventory quantities; they are maintained separately (cycle counts).

steps.name: Review reorder / safety stock
steps.note: 60 sellable products below reorder point, 122 below safety stock (current snapshot).

steps.name: Archive old transactions
steps.note: Archive covers 2011-04-16..2013-07-30, current 2013-07-31..2014-08-03: a clean date cut-over.

processes.state_entity: Production.Product stock level vs ReorderPoint / SafetyStockLevel (derived)

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> OK
    OK --> Reorder: on hand < ReorderPoint
    Reorder --> BelowSafety: on hand < SafetyStockLevel

processes.flowchart:
flowchart LR
  S[Sales line] -->|trigger: S| TH[(TransactionHistory)]
  P[PO receipt] -->|trigger: P| TH
  W[Work order] -->|trigger: W| TH

  A([Shopper received order]) --> B[Write review: rating, comment]
  B --> C[(ProductReview)]
  C --> D[Product detail shows reviews + average]
  A -. inferred .-> R[Return request - no table]

evidence.note: no order is Cancelled (6) or Rejected (4)

access_patterns.question: Show / add reviews for a product

gaps: Reviews: CAT-11 is designed (REVIEW# items under the product) but product detail neither shows nor accepts reviews.
Returns: would be a net-new DynamoDB entity (RMA under ORDER#), not a migration of existing data.

chapter2_candidates.name: Back-office order fulfilment (approve → pick → ship, cancel)
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Closes the loop on orders placed in the new shop (they sit at status 1 today). Shows the sparse ORDERSTATUS GSI, a TransactWriteItems status change + stock decrement + S transaction, CDC to the before app and zero-ETL to Redshift in one click.

chapter2_candidates.name: Real pricing at checkout: special offers, tax by state, ship-method freight
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Replaces demo 8%/2.5% with the real tables; a new promotion immediately changes shop prices; shows denormalised offer items on the product partition.

chapter2_candidates.name: Procurement workspace: low-stock → suggested PO → approve → receive
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: A whole new domain (aw-purchasing) going live with no UI before; the reorder → vendor → PO → receipt chain is a story business stakeholders understand; status machine with partial receipts and rejects.

chapter2_candidates.name: Product reviews on product detail
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Cheap, visible shopper feature; one-partition read with the product; good warm-up for a write path through CDC.

chapter2_candidates.name: Production floor: open work orders, routing timeline, BOM explorer, scrap
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Shows the 'hard' patterns solved in DynamoDB (recursive BOM, where-used) and a visual routing Gantt; strong technical showcase.

chapter2_candidates.name: Sales-person workspace: my stores, reseller order entry by PO number, quota attainment
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Mixes DynamoDB operational reads with a Redshift attainment tile (D7 split in action).

chapter2_candidates.name: Customer self-service profile (addresses, cards, email opt-in)
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Lets a shopper add a ship-to address before checkout; small but completes the shopper journey.

chapter2_candidates.name: Analytics additions: promotion effectiveness, vendor performance, production scrap/on-time
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: New Redshift views over zero-ETL data that AdventureWorksDW never had: shows the warehouse is more than a DW rebuild.

chapter2_candidates.name: HR: employee directory + org chart
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Hierarchy via materialised path is a nice pattern, but HR is far from the shop story.

chapter2_candidates.name: Returns / RMA
chapter2_candidates.demo_value: Net-new data model (no source data); only worth it to show green-field DynamoDB design after migration.
